title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 102 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 533–539 (Night 102, continuing directly from nights-101), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 102 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The storyteller explains why the Muslims were near defeat: Dhāt al-Dawāhī had gone to the walls of Constantinople and had a letter drawn up on a rope to King Afrīdūn, boasting that she had captured the sultan and his vizier and drawn off part of the besiegers, and urging an all-out sortie. The Christian army falls on the camp; the chamberlain holds through a night and a day until Sharrukān, Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the vizier Dandān and the Daylamite emirs arrive and turn the battle. An old monk then rides over with Afrīdūn's offer to settle the war by single combat, and Sharrukān accepts. Next morning the two champions fight until the sun begins to yellow; Afrīdūn tricks Sharrukān into looking behind him, throws his lance, and Sharrukān falls senseless, and the vizier Dandān is the first to reach him. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and second night,
sentences.n: The night is numbered “the second after the hundred”, the hundred and second. al-thāniya is the ordinal “second”; the print spells miʾa “hundred” with an alif, مائة, the old spelling, and the alif is not pronounced.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ لَمَّا أَدْرَكَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهُمْ فِي حَالَةِ الِانْكِسَارِ وَالْحَاجِبُ قَدْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَى الْهَزِيمَةِ وَالْفِرَارِ وَالسَّيْفُ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ الْأَبْرَارِ وَالْفُجَّارِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna sharrukāna lammā adraka al-muslimīna wa-hum fī ḥālati al-inkisāri wa-al-ḥājibu qad ashrafa ʿalā al-hazīmati wa-al-firāri wa-al-sayfu yaʿmalu bayna al-abrāri wa-al-fujjāri
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Sharrukān, when he overtook the Muslims, and they in a state of the breaking, and the chamberlain had come to the edge of the rout and the flight, and the sword working among the righteous and the wicked —
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Sharrukān came up with the Muslims, they were already broken, the chamberlain on the brink of defeat and flight, and the sword at work among good men and bad alike.
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and ان together (السعيدان). The edition often sets two words as one, or splits one; the spacing is kept as printed throughout, and the pointing reads the words as they should be divided. Shahrazād takes up the scene where the last night ended, in the same rhymed words: al-inkisār / al-firār / al-fujjār. The “when” clause is left hanging: before saying what Sharrukān did, the storyteller breaks off to explain how the Muslims came to be in this state. The shadda on الفجّار is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ السَّبَبُ فِي خَذْلِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنَّ اللَّعِينَةَ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي عَدُوَّةَ الدِّينِ لَمَّارَأَتْ بَهْرَامَ وَرُسْتُمَ قَدْ سَارَا بِعَسْكَرِهِمَا نَحْوَ شَرْكَانَ وَأَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ سَارَتْ هِيَ نَحْوَ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَنْفَذَتِ الْأَمِيرَ تُرْكَاشَ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-sababu fī khadhli al-muslimīna anna al-laʿīnata dhāta al-dawāhī ʿaduwwata al-dīni lammā raʾat bahrāma wa-rustama qad sārā bi-ʿaskarihimā naḥwa sharrukāna wa-akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni sārat hiya naḥwa ʿaskari al-muslimīna wa-anfadhati al-amīra turkāsha kamā taqaddama dhikruhu
sentences.l: And the cause of the abandoning of the Muslims was that the accursed one, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, the enemy of the faith, when she saw Bahrām and Rustam had gone with their army toward Sharrukān and his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, went, she, toward the army of the Muslims, and sent-off the emir Turkāsh, as the mention of it has gone before.
sentences.i: The reason the Muslims had been left in such straits was this: when the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī, that enemy of the faith, saw that Bahrām and Rustam had marched with their army toward Sharrukān and his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, she went herself to the Muslim army and had the emir Turkāsh sent off, as was told before.
sentences.n: The print sets لما and رأت as one word, لمارأت; the spacing is kept. The shadda on عدوّة is the print’s, and the ة at its end is the feminine: “enemy” agrees with the old woman. khadhl is leaving someone in the lurch: the Muslims had been stripped of support and left weak. anfadha, “send off, dispatch”: she had talked the besiegers into sending Turkāsh away with a large detachment.

sentences.t: وَقَصْدُهَا بِذَلِكَ أَنْ تُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يَضْعُفُوا
sentences.tr: wa-qaṣduhā bi-dhālika an tufarriqa bayna ʿaskari al-muslimīna li-ajli an yaḍʿufū
sentences.l: And her aim by that was that she divide among the army of the Muslims, for the sake that they grow-weak.
sentences.i: Her purpose in this was to split the Muslim army, so that they would be weakened.
sentences.n: li-ajli an, “for the sake of, in order that”: li- “for” + ajl “sake”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَرَكَتْهُمْ وَقَصَدَتِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ وَنَادَتْ بَطَارِقَةَ الرُّومِ بِأَعْلَى صَوْتِهَا وَقَالَتْ أَدْلُوا حَبْلًا لِاَرْبِطَ فِيهِ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ وَأَوْصِلُوهُ إِلَى مَلِكِكُمْ أَفْرِيدُونَ لِيَقْرَأَهُ هُوَ وَوَلَدِي مَلِكُ الرُّومِ وَيَعْمَلَا بِمَا فِيهِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ وَنَوَاهِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma tarakathum wa-qaṣadati al-qusṭanṭīniyyata wa-nādat baṭāriqata al-rūmi bi-aʿlā ṣawtihā wa-qālat adlū ḥablan li-arbiṭa fīhi hādhā al-kitāba wa-awṣilūhu ilā malikikum afrīdūna li-yaqraʾahu huwa wa-waladī maliku al-rūmi wa-yaʿmalā bi-mā fīhi min amrihi wa-nawāhīhi
sentences.l: Then she left them and made for Constantinople, and called the patricians of the Rūm with the highest of her voice, and said: Let down a rope, that I may tie in it this letter, and convey it to your king Afrīdūn, that he read it, he and my son the king of the Rūm, and the two act by what is in it of its bidding and its forbiddings.
sentences.i: Then she left them and made for Constantinople, and called up to the patricians of the Rūm at the top of her voice, “Let down a rope so that I can tie this letter to it, and take it to your king Afrīdūn, so that he and my son, the king of the Rūm, may read it and do as it bids and forbids.”
sentences.n: baṭāriqa, “patricians”, are the Byzantine high officers. The kasra and fatḥa on لِاَربط are the print’s: li- “so that”, with the verb in the subjunctive. yaʿmalā is dual, “the two of them act”, and ʿamila bi- is “act upon”: the verb chooses the bi-. amr … nawāhī pairs “command” with “prohibitions” (sing. nāhiya): orders of every kind.

sentences.t: فَأَدْلَوْا إِلَيْهَا حَبْلًا فَرَبَطَتْ فِيهِ الْكِتَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-adlaw ilayhā ḥablan fa-rabaṭat fīhi al-kitāba
sentences.l: So they let down to her a rope, and she tied in it the letter.
sentences.i: So they let a rope down to her, and she tied the letter to it.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ مَضْمُونُهُ مِنْ عِنْدِ الدَّاهِيَةِ الْعُظْمَى وَالطَّامَّةِ الْكُبْرَى ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna maḍmūnuhu min ʿindi al-dāhiyati al-ʿuẓmā wa-al-ṭāmmati al-kubrā dhāti al-dawāhī ilā al-maliki afrīdūna
sentences.l: And its content was: From the presence of the calamity the greatest and the catastrophe the biggest, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, to the king Afrīdūn.
sentences.i: This is what it said: From the greatest of calamities and the supreme catastrophe, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, to King Afrīdūn.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-ʿuẓmā / al-kubrā. The old woman signs herself as a disaster, punning on her own name, “She of the Calamities”; al-ṭāmma al-kubrā, “the great catastrophe”, is also a Qurʾānic name for the Last Day (79:34). The shadda on الطامّة is the print’s.

sentences.t: أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنِّي دَبَّرْتُ لَكُمْ حِيلَةً عَلَى هَلَاكِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَكُونُوا مُطْمَئِّنِينَ
sentences.tr: ammā baʿdu fa-innī dabbartu lakum ḥīlatan ʿalā halāki al-muslimīna fa-kūnū muṭmaʾinnīna
sentences.l: As for after: I have contrived for you a stratagem for the destruction of the Muslims, so be at-ease.
sentences.i: To proceed: I have devised a stratagem for you to destroy the Muslims, so rest easy.
sentences.n: ammā baʿdu, “as for what follows”, is the fixed formula that opens the body of a letter. The shadda on دبّرت is the print’s. In مطمئّنين the print sets its shadda on the hamza instead of the nūn; it is kept where the print has it, but the word is muṭmaʾinnīn, “at ease, reassured”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَسَرْتُهُمْ وَأَسَرْتُ سُلْطَانَهُمْ وَوَزِيرَهُمْ ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى عَسْكَرِهِمْ وَأَخْبَرْتُهُمْ بِذَلِكَ فَانْكَسَرَتْ شَوْكَتُهُمْ وَضَعُفَتْ قُوَّتُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qad asartuhum wa-asartu sulṭānahum wa-wazīrahum thumma tawajjahtu ilā ʿaskarihim wa-akhbartuhum bi-dhālika fa-inkasarat shawkatuhum wa-ḍaʿufat quwwatuhum
sentences.l: And I have captured them, and captured their sultan and their vizier; then I turned to their army and informed them of that, so their thorn broke and their strength grew-weak.
sentences.i: I have taken them captive, their sultan and their vizier among them; then I went to their army and told them of it, and their spirit broke and their strength failed.
sentences.n: The shadda on توجّهت is the print’s. shawka, literally “thorn”, is a fighting force’s sting: “their thorn broke” means their power to fight was gone. akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَدَعْتُ الْعَسْكَرَ الْمُحَاصِرِينَ لِلْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ حَتَّى أَرْسَلْتُ اثْنَا عَشَرَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ مَعَ الْأَمِيرِ تُرْكَاشَ خِلَافَ الْمَأْسُورِينَ وَمَا بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا الْقَلِيلُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad khadaʿtu al-ʿaskara al-muḥāṣirīna li-al-qusṭanṭīniyyati ḥattā arsaltu ithnā ʿashara alfa fārisin maʿa al-amīri turkāsha khilāfa al-maʾsūrīna wa-mā baqiya minhum illā al-qalīlu
sentences.l: And I have deceived the army, the besiegers of Constantinople, until I sent twelve thousand horsemen with the emir Turkāsh, apart-from the captured-ones, and there remained not of them except the few.
sentences.i: And I have tricked the army besieging Constantinople, so that I got twelve thousand horsemen sent off with the emir Turkāsh, besides those taken captive, and only a few of them are left.
sentences.n: al-ʿaskar, “the army”, is singular but takes a plural adjective, al-muḥāṣirīna, agreeing with the men in it; al-muḥāṣirīna li-, “besieging”: the li- marks the object of the participle. ithnā ʿashara, “twelve”, stands in the nominative form where, as the object of “I sent”, Classical Arabic wants ithnay ʿashara: a Middle Arabic habit, kept. khilāfa, “apart from, besides”.

sentences.t: فَالْمُرَادُ مِنْكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِجَمِيعِ عَسْكَرِكُمْ فِي بَقِيَّةِ هَذَا النَّهَارِ وَتَهْجُمُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي خِيَامِهِمْ وَلَكِنَّكُمْ لَا تَخْرُجُونَ إِلَّا سَوَاءً وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-al-murādu minkum annakum takhrujūna ilayhim bi-jamīʿi ʿaskarikum fī baqiyyati hādhā al-nahāri wa-tahjumūna ʿalayhim fī khiyāmihim wa-lākinnakum lā takhrujūna illā sawāʾan wa-uqtulūhum ʿan ākhirihim
sentences.l: So the wanted-thing from you is that you go out to them with all of your army in the remainder of this day, and fall upon them in their tents; but you go not out except together, and kill them to the last of them.
sentences.i: So what I want of you is this: march out against them with your whole army in what is left of today, and fall upon them in their tents; but go out all together, and kill them to the last man.
sentences.n: The shaddas on انّكم, بقيّة and ولكنّكم are the print’s. The print has الا سواء as two words; read as illā sawāʾan, “only all together, as one body”, the likeliest sense, though the phrase is unusual and the reading uncertain. The letter slips from “you will go out” into a plain command, “kill them”. ʿan ākhirihim, “down to the last of them”.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْمَسِيحَ قَدْ نَظَرَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَالْعَذْرَاءَ تَعَطَّفَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-masīḥa qad naẓara ilaykum wa-al-ʿadhrāʾa taʿaṭṭafat ʿalaykum
sentences.l: For the Messiah has looked toward you, and the Virgin has inclined-in-kindness toward you.
sentences.i: For the Messiah has looked upon you, and the Virgin has taken pity on you.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: ilaykum / ʿalaykum. The shaddas on فانّ and تعطّفت are the print’s. al-ʿAdhrāʾ, “the Virgin”, is Mary.

sentences.t: وَأَرْجُو مِنَ الْمَسِيحِ أَنْ لَايَنْسَى فِعْلِي الَّذِي قَدْ فَعَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-arjū mina al-masīḥi an lā yansā fiʿlī alladhī qad faʿaltuhu
sentences.l: And I hope from the Messiah that he not forget my deed which I have done.
sentences.i: And I hope the Messiah will not forget what I have done.
sentences.n: The print runs لا and ينسى together, لاينسى; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ كِتَابُهَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ فَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَأَرْسَلَ فِي الْحَالِ إِلَى مَلِكِ الرُّومِ ابْنِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي وَأَحْضَرَهُ وَقَرَأَ الْكِتَابَ عَلَيْهِ فَفَرِحَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala kitābuhā ilā al-maliki afrīdūna fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan wa-arsala fī al-ḥāli ilā maliki al-rūmi ibni dhāti al-dawāhī wa-aḥḍarahu wa-qaraʾa al-kitāba ʿalayhi fa-fariḥa
sentences.l: And when her letter reached the king Afrīdūn, he rejoiced a rejoicing intense, and sent in the moment to the king of the Rūm, the son of Dhāt al-Dawāhī, and had him brought, and read the letter to him, and he rejoiced.
sentences.i: When her letter reached King Afrīdūn he was overjoyed; he sent at once for the king of the Rūm, Dhāt al-Dawāhī’s son, had him brought in and read him the letter, and he too rejoiced.
sentences.n: faraḥan shadīdan, “a great joy”: the verbal noun repeats the verb to intensify it. qaraʾa ʿalā, “read out to”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ انْظُرْ مَكْرَأُمِّي فَإِنَّهُ يُغْنِى عَنِ السُّيُوفِ وَطَلْعَتُهَا تَنُوبُ عَنْ هَوْلِ الْيَوْمِ الْمَخُوفِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla unẓur makra ummī fa-innahu yughnī ʿani al-suyūfi wa-ṭalʿatuhā tanūbu ʿan hawli al-yawmi al-makhūfi
sentences.l: And he said: Look at the cunning of my mother, for it makes-needless the swords, and her countenance stands-in for the terror of the day the dreaded.
sentences.i: And he said, “See my mother’s cunning! It does the work of swords, and the mere sight of her serves in place of the terrors of a dreadful day of battle.”
sentences.n: The print runs مكر and امّي together, مكرامّي, “my mother’s cunning”; the spacing is kept, and the shadda is the print’s. It writes يغنى with a final ى for ي, a habit of the edition. Rhymed prose: al-suyūf / al-makhūf. aghnā ʿan, “make unnecessary, do instead of”; nāba ʿan, “stand in for”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ لَاعَدِمَ الْمَسِيحُ طَلْعَةَ أُمِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku afrīdūnu lā ʿadima al-masīḥu ṭalʿata ummika
sentences.l: And the king Afrīdūn said: May the Messiah not be bereft of the countenance of your mother.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn said, “May the Messiah never be without your mother’s face!”
sentences.n: The print runs لا and عدم together, لاعدم; the spacing is kept. lā with the past tense makes a wish: “may X never be deprived of Y” is a way of praising Y as a treasure. ṭalʿa, “face, countenance”, takes up the son’s word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَمَرَ الْبَطَارِقَةَ أَنْ يُنَادُوا بِالرَّحِيلِ إِلَى خَارِجِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu amara al-baṭāriqata an yunādū bi-al-raḥīli ilā khāriji al-madīnati
sentences.l: Then he commanded the patricians that they proclaim the departure to the outside of the city.
sentences.i: Then he ordered the patricians to proclaim the march out of the city.
sentences.n: nādā bi-, “proclaim, cry out”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: وَشَاعَ الْخَبَرُ فِى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَخَرَجَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ النَّصْرَانِيَّةُ وَالْعِصَابَةُ الصَّلِيبِيَّةُ وَجَرَّدُوا السُّيُوفَ الْحِدَادَ وَأَعْلَنُوا بِكَلِمَةِ الْكُفْرِ وَالْإِلْحَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-shāʿa al-khabaru fī al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-kharajati al-ʿasākiru al-naṣrāniyyatu wa-al-ʿiṣābatu al-ṣalībiyyatu wa-jarradū al-suyūfa al-ḥidāda wa-aʿlanū bi-kalimati al-kufri wa-al-ilḥādi
sentences.l: And the news spread in Constantinople, and the armies the Christian and the band the Cross-bearing went out, and they bared the swords the sharp, and proclaimed the word of the unbelief and the heresy.
sentences.i: The news spread through Constantinople, and the Christian armies and the host of the Cross marched out, drew their sharp swords and loudly declared their creed of unbelief and heresy.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-naṣrāniyya / al-ṣalībiyya, then al-ḥidād / al-ilḥād. The narrator speaks from the Muslim side throughout. The shadda on جرّدوا is the print’s, and the print writes فى with ى for ي. aʿlana bi-, “declare openly”: the bi- marks what is declared.

sentences.t: وَكَفَرُوا بِرَبِّ الْعِبَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-kafarū bi-rabbi al-ʿibādi
sentences.l: and they disbelieved in the Lord of the servants.
sentences.i: and renounced the Lord of all mankind.
sentences.n: This clause ends the description of the Christian army begun before: they came out with drawn swords, proclaiming their unbelief. kafara bi-, “disbelieve in”: the verb chooses the bi-, which marks what is denied.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ الْحَاجِبُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ قَالَ إِنَّ الرُّومَ قَدْ وَصَلُوا إِلَيْنَا وَقَدْ عَلِمُوا أَنَّ سُلْطَانَنَا غَائِبٌ فَرُبَّمَا هَجَمُوا عَلَيْنَا وَأَكْثَرُ عَسْكَرِنَا قَدْ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-ḥājibu ilā dhālika qāla inna al-rūma qad waṣalū ilaynā wa-qad ʿalimū anna sulṭānanā ghāʾibun fa-rubbamā hajamū ʿalaynā wa-aktharu ʿaskarinā qad tawajjaha ilā al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain looked at that, he said: The Rūm have reached us, and they have learned that our sultan is absent; so perhaps they will fall upon us, and most of our army has gone off to King Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain saw this, he said, “The Rūm are upon us, and they know our sultan is away. They may well attack us, with most of our army gone off to King Ḍawʾ al-Makān.”
sentences.n: wa-aktharu ʿaskarinā …, “while most of our army …”: a circumstantial clause introduced by wa-. The shadda on توجّه is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَاغْتَاظَ الْحَاجِبُ وَنَادَى يَاعَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَحُمَاةَ الدِّينِ الْمَتِينِ إِنْ هَرَبْتُمْ هَلَكْتُمْ وَإِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ نُصِرْتُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ightāẓa al-ḥājibu wa-nādā yā ʿaskara al-muslimīna wa-ḥumāta al-dīni al-matīni in harabtum halaktum wa-in ṣabartum nuṣirtum
sentences.l: And the chamberlain grew-angry and called out: O army of the Muslims, and protectors of the firm religion! If you flee, you perish, and if you endure, you are given-victory.
sentences.i: The chamberlain was enraged and cried out, “Army of the Muslims, defenders of the steadfast faith! Flee and you perish; stand firm and you will be granted victory.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: halaktum / nuṣirtum. The print sets يا and عسكر as one word, ياعسكر. The ḍamma on حُماة is the print’s. After in, “if”, both verbs are perfect but the sense is future.

sentences.t: فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الشَّجَاعَةَ صَبْرُ سَاعَةٍ وَمَاضَاقَ أَمْرٌإِلَّا أَوْجَدَ اللَّهُ اتِّسَاعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-iʿlamū anna al-shajāʿata ṣabru sāʿatin wa-mā ḍāqa amrun illā awjada allāhu ittisāʿahu
sentences.l: So know that courage is the endurance of an hour, and no matter grew-narrow but God brought-into-being its widening.
sentences.i: Know that courage is but an hour’s endurance, and no strait ever closed in but God opened a way out of it.
sentences.n: A proverb, rhymed: shajāʿa / sāʿa. mā … illā, “not … except”: every narrow pass is followed by relief. The print runs two pairs of words together, وماضاق (wa-mā ḍāqa) and امرالّا (amrun illā); the shadda on الّا is the print’s.

sentences.t: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكُمْ وَنَظَرَ إِلَيْكُمْ بِعَيْنِ الرَّحْمَةِ
sentences.tr: bāraka allāhu fīkum wa-naẓara ilaykum bi-ʿayni al-raḥmati
sentences.l: May God bless in you, and look at you with the eye of mercy!”
sentences.i: God bless you and look on you with the eye of mercy!”
sentences.n: Perfect verbs in a blessing are wishes: bāraka allāhu, “may God bless”. bi-ʿayni, “with the eye of”: the bi- is instrumental.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ كَبَّرَتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَصَاحَتِ الْمُوَحِّدُونَ وَدَارَتْ رَحَاةُ الْحَرْبِ بِالطَّعْنِ وَالضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika kabbarati al-muslimūna wa-ṣāḥati al-muwaḥḥidūna wa-dārat raḥātu al-ḥarbi bi-al-ṭaʿni wa-al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And at that the Muslims cried God-is-greatest, and the professors-of-oneness shouted, and the millstone of war turned with the thrusting and the smiting.
sentences.i: At that the Muslims raised the cry “God is greatest,” the believers in the One God shouted, and the millstone of war began to turn with thrust and blow.
sentences.n: kabbara is to cry Allāhu akbar. Feminine verbs (kabbarat, ṣāḥat) with a masculine sound plural subject are not Classical; the text treats such plurals as collectives, and does so again below. The print has رحاة, for رحى, “millstone”, the usual image of war grinding men; we read it as raḥāt. Rhymed prose: ṭaʿn / ḍarb. The shaddas on كبّرت and الموحّدون are the print’s.

sentences.t: وَعَمِلَتِ الصَّوَارِمُ وَالرِّمَاحُ وَمَلَأَ الدَّمُ الْأَوْدِيَةَ وَالْبِطَاحَ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿamilati al-ṣawārimu wa-al-rimāḥu wa-malaʾa al-damu al-awdiyata wa-al-biṭāḥa
sentences.l: And the sharp-swords and the spears worked, and the blood filled the valleys and the plains.
sentences.i: Swords and spears did their work, and blood filled the valleys and the plains.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: rimāḥ / biṭāḥ. ṣārim, plural ṣawārim, is a sharp, cutting sword.

sentences.t: وَتَسَسَّتِ الْقُسُوسُ وَالرُّهْبَانُ وَشَدُّوا الزَّنَانِيرَ وَرَفَعُوا الصُّلْبَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-tasassati al-qusūsu wa-al-ruhbānu wa-shaddū al-zanānīra wa-rafaʿū al-ṣulbāna
sentences.l: And the priests and the monks [made ready?], and they bound the girdles and raised the crosses.
sentences.i: The priests and monks took up their office, girded on their belts and raised their crosses.
sentences.n: The print has تسست, which is obscure. It may stand for تقسّست, “they acted as priests”, or تنسّكت, “they devoted themselves to worship”; neither is certain, and our pointing tasassat is only a guess at the printed letters. The zunnār is the girdle Christians were required to wear under Muslim rule.

sentences.t: وَأَعْلَنَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ بِتَكْبِيرِ الْمَلِكِ الدَّيَّانِ وَصَاحُوا بِتِلَاوَةِ الْقُرْآنِ وَاصْطَدَمَ حِزْبُ الرَّحْمٰنِ بِحِزْبِ الشَّيْطَانِ وَطَارَتِ الرُّؤُسُ عَنِ الْأَبْدَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿlana al-muslimūna bi-takbīri al-maliki al-dayyāni wa-ṣāḥū bi-tilāwati al-qurʾāni wa-iṣṭadama ḥizbu al-raḥmāni bi-ḥizbi al-shayṭāni wa-ṭārati al-ruʾūsu ʿani al-abdāni
sentences.l: And the Muslims proclaimed the magnifying of the King, the Judge, and shouted with the reciting of the Qurʾān; and the party of the Merciful clashed with the party of Satan, and the heads flew from the bodies.
sentences.i: The Muslims loudly magnified God, the King who judges all, and shouted out verses of the Qurʾān; the party of the Merciful clashed with the party of Satan, and heads flew from bodies.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: dayyān / qurʾān / raḥmān / shayṭān / abdān. aʿlana bi-, “proclaim aloud”: the bi- marks what is proclaimed; ṣāḥa bi- likewise, “cry out”; iṣṭadama bi-, “collide with”. The print spells ruʾūs, “heads”, as رؤس, without the second wāw.

sentences.t: وَطَافَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْأَخْيَارُ عَلَى أُمَّةِ النَّبِيِّ الْمُخْتَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭāfati al-malāʾikatu al-akhyāru ʿalā ummati al-nabiyyi al-mukhtāri
sentences.l: And the good angels went-round over the community of the Chosen Prophet.
sentences.i: The goodly angels hovered over the community of the Chosen Prophet.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: akhyār / mukhtār. ṭāfa ʿalā, “go round about, attend”: here the angels circle over the Muslims to aid them.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ السَّيْفُ يَعْمَلُ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-sayfu yaʿmalu ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And the sword did not cease working until the day turned-away and the night came on with the darkening.
sentences.i: The sword never ceased its work until the day departed and night came on in deepening dark.
sentences.n: lam yazal + imperfect, “kept on doing”. Rhymed prose: nahār / iʿtikār. aqbala bi-, “come on with”: the bi- marks what the night brings. The shadda on ولّى is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَحَاطَتِ الْكُفَّارُ بِالْمُسْلِمِينَ وَحَسِبُوا أَنْ يَنْجُوا مِنَ الْعَذَابِ الْمُهِينِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad aḥāṭati al-kuffāru bi-al-muslimīna wa-ḥasibū an yanjū mina al-ʿadhābi al-muhīni
sentences.l: And the unbelievers had surrounded the Muslims, and they reckoned to escape from the shameful torment.
sentences.i: By now the unbelievers had surrounded the Muslims and thought they would escape the shameful torment.
sentences.n: The print has يبخوا, a misprint for ينجوا, corrected here. aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”: the verb chooses the bi-. The subject of ḥasibū is not stated; most likely the unbelievers, now sure they would not be defeated, al-ʿadhāb al-muhīn being the Qurʾān’s phrase for the punishment of unbelievers. The shadda on الكفّار is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَطَمِعَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ فِي أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ إِلَى أَنْ طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ وَبَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭamiʿa al-mushrikūna fī ahli al-īmāni ilā an ṭalaʿa al-fajru wa-bāna
sentences.l: And the associators coveted the people of the faith, until the dawn rose and appeared.
sentences.i: The idolaters had their hopes set on the people of faith until dawn rose and broke clear.
sentences.n: The print has اى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. ṭamiʿa fī, “covet, set one’s hopes on”: the verb chooses the fī. mushrik, “one who associates partners with God”, is the polemical name for the Christians here. Rhymed prose: īmān / bān.

sentences.t: فَرَكِبَ الْحَاجِبُ هُوَ وَعَسْكَرُهُ وَرَجَا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَنْصُرُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-rakiba al-ḥājibu huwa wa-ʿaskaruhu wa-rajā anna allāha yanṣuruhu
sentences.l: And the chamberlain rode, he and his army, and hoped that God would give-him-victory.
sentences.i: The chamberlain mounted with his army, hoping that God would grant him victory.
sentences.n: rakiba huwa wa-ʿaskaruhu: the pronoun huwa is repeated so that “and his army” can be joined to the verb’s subject.

sentences.t: وَاخْتَلَطَتِ الْأُمَمُ بِالْأُمَمِ وَقَامَتِ الْحَرْبُ عَلَى قَدَمٍ وَطَارَتِ الْقِمَمُ
sentences.tr: wa-ikhtalaṭati al-umamu bi-al-umami wa-qāmati al-ḥarbu ʿalā qadamin wa-ṭārati al-qimamu
sentences.l: And the nations mixed with the nations, and the war stood up on a foot, and the skulls flew.
sentences.i: Nation closed with nation, the battle rose to its full height, and heads went flying.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: umam / qadam / qimam. qāmat al-ḥarb ʿalā qadam, “war stood on its foot”, is a set phrase for battle at its height. ikhtalaṭa bi-, “mingle with”: the bi- marks the other party.

sentences.t: وَثَبَتَ الشُّجَاعُ وَتَقَدَّمَ وَوَلَّى الْجَبَانُ وَانْهَزَمَ وَقَضَى قَاضِى الْمَوْتِ وَحَكَمَ حَتَّى تَطَاوَحَتِ الْأَبْطَالُ عَنِ السُّرُوجِ وَامْتَلَأَتْ بِالْأَمْوَاتِ الْمُرُوجُ
sentences.tr: wa-thabata al-shujāʿu wa-taqaddama wa-wallā al-jabānu wa-inhazama wa-qaḍā qāḍī al-mawti wa-ḥakama ḥattā taṭāwaḥati al-abṭālu ʿani al-surūji wa-imtalaʾat bi-al-amwāti al-murūju
sentences.l: And the brave-one stood-firm and advanced, and the coward turned-away and was routed, and the judge of death judged and ruled, until the champions were flung from the saddles, and the meadows were filled with the dead.
sentences.i: The brave stood firm and pressed forward, the coward turned his back and fled, and Death the judge passed sentence and gave his ruling, until champions were hurled from their saddles and the meadows were filled with the dead.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: taqaddam / inhazam / ḥakam, then surūj / murūj. The print has تطاوحت; the usual form is تطايحت, “were flung about” (from ṭāḥa, ṭawwaḥa, “fling”), and the printed letters are kept, read in that sense. قاضى is written with ى for final ي, the print’s habit. imtalaʾa bi-, “be filled with”: the bi- marks the contents. The shaddas on تقدّم and ولّى are the print’s.

sentences.t: وَتَأَخَّرَتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَنْ أَمَاكِنِهِمْ وَمَلَكَتِ الرُّومُ بَعْضَ خِيَامِهِمْ وَمَسَاكِنِهَا وَعَزَمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى الِانْكِسَارِ وَالْهَزِيمَةِ وَالْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-taʾakhkharati al-muslimūna ʿan amākinihim wa-malakati al-rūmu baʿḍa khiyāmihim wa-masākinihā wa-ʿazama al-muslimūna ʿalā al-inkisāri wa-al-hazīmati wa-al-firāri
sentences.l: And the Muslims fell-back from their places, and the Rūm took-possession of some of their tents and its dwellings, and the Muslims resolved on breaking and defeat and flight.
sentences.i: The Muslims fell back from their positions, the Rūm seized some of their tents and quarters, and the Muslims were on the point of breaking and fleeing in defeat.
sentences.n: masākinihā, “its dwellings”: the -hā has no clear antecedent; it may refer to the army as a feminine collective, or simply be loose for masākinihim. ʿazama ʿalā, “resolve on”: here less a decision than the brink of it.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ وَصَلَ شَرْكَانُ بِعَسَاكِرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَرَايَاتِ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamāhum ka-dhālika idh waṣala sharrukānu bi-ʿasākiri al-muslimīna wa-rāyāti al-muwaḥḥidīna
sentences.l: And while they were like that, behold, Sharrukān arrived with the armies of the Muslims and the banners of the professors-of-oneness.
sentences.i: While they were in this plight, Sharrukān suddenly arrived with the Muslim armies and the banners of the believers in the One God.
sentences.n: baynamā … idh, “while … suddenly”: the idh marks the surprise. The print sets فبينماهم as one word. waṣala bi-, “arrive with, bring”: the bi- marks what is brought.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ شَرْكَانُ حَمَلَ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ وَتَبِعَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَحَمَلَ بَعْدَهُمَا الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَكَذَلِكَ أَمِيرُ الدَّيْلَمِ بَهْرَامُ وَرُسْتُمُ وَأَخُوهُ تُرْكَاشُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala ʿalayhim sharrukānu ḥamala ʿalā al-kuffāri wa-tabiʿahu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-ḥamala baʿdahumā al-wazīru dandānu wa-ka-dhālika amīru al-daylami bahrāmu wa-rustamu wa-akhūhu turkāshu
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān came upon them, he charged on the unbelievers, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān followed him, and after the two of them charged the vizier Dandān, and likewise the emir of the Daylam, Bahrām, and Rustam and his brother Turkāsh.
sentences.i: As soon as Sharrukān reached them he charged the unbelievers, with Ḍawʾ al-Makān behind him; after the two of them the vizier Dandān charged, and so did Bahrām, emir of the Daylam, and Rustam, and Bahrām’s brother Turkāsh.
sentences.n: ḥamala ʿalā, “charge”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. The Daylam are the people of the highlands south of the Caspian. akhūhu, “his brother”: Turkāsh is Bahrām’s brother, as the previous night says. The shaddas on فلمّا and الكفّار are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا ذَلِكَ طَارَتْ عُقُولُهُمْ وَغُلِبَ مَعْقُولُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-innahum lammā raʾaw dhālika ṭārat ʿuqūluhum wa-ghuliba maʿqūluhum
sentences.l: For they, when they saw that, their minds flew, and their reason was overcome.
sentences.i: When the enemy saw this, their wits flew from them and their reason failed.
sentences.n: “They” are the Rūm. Rhymed prose: ʿuqūluhum / maʿqūluhum. The print writes رأوا as راوا, with no hamza. The shadda on لمّا is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَثَارَ الْغُبَارُ حَتَّى مَلَأَ الْأَقْطَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-thāra al-ghubāru ḥattā malaʾa al-aqṭāra
sentences.l: And the dust rose until it filled the regions.
sentences.i: The dust rose until it filled every quarter.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: ghubār / aqṭār.

sentences.t: وَاجْتَمَعَتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ الْأَخْيَارُ بِأَصْحَابِهِمُ الْأَبْرَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ijtamaʿati al-muslimūna al-akhyāru bi-aṣḥābihimu al-abrāri
sentences.l: And the good Muslims met with their pious companions.
sentences.i: The good Muslims were reunited with their pious comrades.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿa bi-, “meet with, join”: the bi- marks the one met. Rhymed prose: akhyār / abrār.

sentences.t: وَاجْتَمَعَ شَرْكَانُ بِالْحَاجِبِ فَشَكَرَةُ عَلَى صَبْرِهِ وَهَنَّأَهُ بِتَائِيدِةِ وَنَصْرِةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ijtamaʿa sharrukānu bi-al-ḥājibi fa-shakarahu ʿalā ṣabrihi wa-hannaʾahu bi-taʾyīdihi wa-naṣrihi
sentences.l: And Sharrukān met with the chamberlain, and thanked him for his endurance, and congratulated him on his being-aided and his victory.
sentences.i: Sharrukān joined the chamberlain, thanked him for holding firm, and congratulated him on the help God had given him and on his victory.
sentences.n: The print writes the pronoun -hu, “him, his”, with ة instead of ه three times here: فشكرة (fa-shakarahu), بتائيدة (bi-taʾyīdihi) and نصرة (naṣrihi). It also spells taʾyīd, “divine support”, as تائيد. hannaʾa bi-, “congratulate on”: the bi- marks the occasion. The shadda on هنّأه is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحَتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَقَوِيَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَحَمَلُوا عَلَى أَعْدَائِهِمْ وَأَخْلَصُوا لِلَّهِ فِي جِهَادِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥati al-muslimūna wa-qawiyat qulūbuhum wa-ḥamalū ʿalā aʿdāʾihim wa-akhlaṣū li-allāhi fī jihādihim
sentences.l: And the Muslims rejoiced, and their hearts grew-strong, and they charged on their enemies and were sincere toward God in their holy-war.
sentences.i: The Muslims rejoiced and took heart; they charged their enemies and gave themselves wholly to God in their holy war.
sentences.n: akhlaṣa li-, “be sincere toward, devote oneself purely to”: the li- marks the one served. The shadda on للّه is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ الْكُفَّارُ إِلَى الرَّايَاتِ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةِ وَعَلَيْهَا كَلِمَةُ الْإِخْلَاصِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةُ صَاحُوا بِالْوَيْلِ وَالثُّبُورِ وَاسْتَغَاثُوا بِبَطَارِقَةِ الدُّيُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-kuffāru ilā al-rāyāti al-muḥammadiyyati wa-ʿalayhā kalimatu al-ikhlāṣi al-islāmiyyatu ṣāḥū bi-al-wayli wa-al-thubūri wa-istaghāthū bi-baṭāriqati al-duyūri
sentences.l: And when the unbelievers looked at the Muhammadan banners, and upon them the word of pure-devotion, the Islamic one, they cried out with woe and destruction and called-for-help to the patriarchs of the monasteries.
sentences.i: When the unbelievers saw the banners of Muhammad, bearing the Muslim profession of God’s oneness, they cried out in woe and ruin and called on the patriarchs of the monasteries for help.
sentences.n: kalimat al-ikhlāṣ, “the word of sincere devotion”, is the profession “There is no god but God”. ṣāḥa bi-al-wayl wa-al-thubūr, “cry woe and ruin”, is a Qurʾānic phrase. istaghātha bi-, “call on for help”: the bi- marks the one appealed to. baṭāriqa is the plural of biṭrīq, here church dignitaries; duyūr is a plural of dayr, “monastery”. Rhymed prose: thubūr / duyūr.

sentences.t: وَنَادَوْا حَنَّى وَمَرْيَمَ وَالصَّلِيبَ الْمُسَخَّمَ وَانْقَبَضَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ عَنِ الْقِتَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-nādaw ḥannā wa-maryama wa-al-ṣalība al-musakhkhama wa-inqabaḍat aydīhim ʿani al-qitāli
sentences.l: And they called on Ḥannā and Mary and the sooty Cross, and their hands drew-back from the fighting.
sentences.i: They called on Ḥannā, on Mary and on the blackened Cross, and their hands shrank from the fight.
sentences.n: The print has حنّى, with its own shadda; the name is obscure. It may be Ḥannā, “John” (from Yūḥannā), or Anne, Mary’s mother; neither is certain. al-ṣalīb al-musakhkham, “the soot-blackened Cross”, is a Muslim jibe at the Christians’ cross.

sentences.t: وَقَدْأَ قْبَلَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ عَلَى مَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَصَارَ أَحَدُهُمَا فِى الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالْآخَرُ فِى الْمَيْسَرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad aqbala al-maliku afrīdūnu ʿalā maliki al-rūmi wa-ṣāra aḥaduhumā fī al-maymanati wa-al-ākharu fī al-maysarati
sentences.l: And King Afrīdūn had come-forward to the king of the Rūm, and one of the two became on the right wing and the other on the left wing.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn had come forward to join the king of the Rūm, and the one took the right wing and the other the left.
sentences.n: The print splits qad aqbala as وقدا قبل: the alif of aqbala, “he came forward”, has slipped onto qad. The words stay as printed and are pointed across the break.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَهُمْ فَارِسٌ مَشْهُورٌ يُسَمَّى لَاوِيَا فَوَقَفَ وَسْطًا
sentences.tr: wa-ʿindahum fārisun mashhūrun yusammā lāwiyā fa-waqafa wasṭan
sentences.l: And with them was a famous horseman who was named Lāwiyā, and he stood in-the-middle.
sentences.i: They had with them a famous knight called Lāwiyā, and he took his stand in the centre.
sentences.n: Lāwiyā appears here for the first time; the print leaves the name unpointed, so its vowels are our guess. The sukūn on wasṭan, “in the middle”, is printed.

sentences.t: وَاصْطَفُّوا لِلنِّزَالِ وَإِنْ كَانُوا فِي فَزَعٍ وَزِلْزَالٍ
sentences.tr: wa-iṣṭaffū li-al-nizāli wa-in kānū fī fazaʿin wa-zilzālin
sentences.l: And they ranged-themselves-in-rows for the combat, even if they were in fright and quaking.
sentences.i: They drew up in their ranks for battle, frightened and shaken though they were.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: nizāl / zilzāl. wa-in, “even if, although”, concedes rather than supposes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَفَّتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَسَاكِرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣaffati al-muslimūna ʿasākirahum
sentences.l: Then the Muslims (she) ranged their armies.
sentences.i: Then the Muslims drew up their own forces.
sentences.n: ṣaffat is feminine although al-muslimūna is a masculine plural: the text treats the host as a collective, a loose agreement common in this Arabic.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْبَلَ شَرْكَانُ عَلَى أَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ لَاشَكَّ أَنَّهُمْ يُرِيدُونَ الْبِرَازَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aqbala sharrukānu ʿalā akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-qāla lahu yā malika al-zamāni lā shakka annahum yurīdūna al-birāza
sentences.l: And at that Sharrukān turned to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him: O king of the age, no doubt that they want the single-combat.
sentences.i: At this Sharrukān turned to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said, “King of the age, there is no doubt they are looking for single combat.
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “turn to, come up to” someone: the verb chooses the ʿalā. al-birāz is fighting man to man between the lines.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا غَايَةُ مُرَادِنَا وَلَكِنْ أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُقَدِّمَ مِنَ الْعَسْكَرِ مَنْ لَهُ عَزْمٌ ثَابِتٌ فَإِنَّ التَّدْبِيرَ نِصْفُ الْمَعِيشَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā ghāyatu murādinā wa-lākin uḥibbu an uqaddima mina al-ʿaskari man lahu ʿazmun thābitun fa-inna al-tadbīra niṣfu al-maʿīshati
sentences.l: And this is the utmost of our desire; but I love that I put-forward from the army whoever to-him is a steadfast resolve, for the planning is half of the livelihood.
sentences.i: That is just what we want; but I would like to send out from the army only men of steadfast resolve, for forethought is half of living.”
sentences.n: “Planning is half of livelihood” is a proverb: good management is half of getting on in the world.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السُّلْطَانُ مَاذَا تُرِيدُيَا صَاحِبَ الرَّأْىِ السَّدِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sulṭānu mādhā turīdu yā ṣāḥiba al-raʾyi al-sadīdi
sentences.l: And the sultan said: What do you want, O owner of the sound opinion?
sentences.i: “What do you have in mind,” said the sultan, “man of sound counsel?”
sentences.n: The print runs turīdu and yā together as one word (تريديا).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ أُرِيدُأَنْ أَكُونَ فِي قَلْبِ عَسْكَرِ الْكُفَّارِ وَأَنْ يَكُونَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ فِى الْمَيْسَرَةِ وَأَنْتَ فِى الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالْأَمِيرُ بَهْرَامُ فِى الْجَنَاحِ الْأَيْمَنِ وَالْأَمِيرُ رُسْتُمُ فِى الْجَنَاحِ الْأَيْسَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu urīdu an akūna fī qalbi ʿaskari al-kuffāri wa-an yakūna al-wazīru dandānu fī al-maysarati wa-anta fī al-maymanati wa-al-amīru bahrāmu fī al-janāḥi al-aymani wa-al-amīru rustamu fī al-janāḥi al-aysari
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: I want that I be in the heart of the army of the infidels, and that the vizier Dandān be on the left wing, and you on the right wing, and the emir Bahrām on the right flank, and the emir Rustam on the left flank.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “I want to take my place facing the centre of the infidel army, with the vizier Dandān on the left and you on the right, the emir Bahrām on the right flank and the emir Rustam on the left.
sentences.n: The print runs urīdu an together (اريدان). The “you” on the right wing sits oddly, since the next sentence puts the sultan himself under the banners; perhaps another commander is meant, but the text says anta.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْعَظِيمُ تَكُونُ تَحْتَ الْأَعْلَامِ وَالرَّايَاتِ لِأَنَّكَ عِمَادُنَا وَعَلَيْكَ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ اعْتِمَادُنَا وَنَحْنُ كُلُّنَا فِدَيٰكَ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ يُؤْذِيكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ayyuhā al-maliku al-ʿaẓīmu takūnu taḥta al-aʿlāmi wa-al-rāyāti li-annaka ʿimādunā wa-ʿalayka baʿda allāhi iʿtimādunā wa-naḥnu kullunā fidāka min kulli amrin yuʾdhīka
sentences.l: And you, O the great king, you will be under the flags and the banners, because you are our pillar, and on you after God is our reliance, and we, all of us, are your ransom from every matter that harms you.
sentences.i: And you, great king, will stay under the flags and banners, for you are our mainstay, and after God our trust is in you; every one of us would give his life to shield you from any harm.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: ʿimādunā / iʿtimādunā, fidāka / yuʾdhīka. The print spells fidāka “your ransom” as فديك, with yāʾ for the long ā (as in Qurʾānic spellings like هُدَىٰهُمْ); the dagger alif gives the sound.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرَةُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarahu ḍawʾu al-makāni ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān thanked him for that.
sentences.n: Again ة for the pronoun -hu (فشكرة, fa-shakarahu).

sentences.t: وَارْتَفَعَ الصِّيَاحُ وَجُرِّدَتِ الصِّفَاحُ
sentences.tr: wa-irtafaʿa al-ṣiyāḥu wa-jurridati al-ṣifāḥu
sentences.l: And the shouting rose, and the broad-blades were bared.
sentences.i: The war cries went up and the swords were drawn.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: ṣiyāḥ / ṣifāḥ. al-ṣifāḥ are broad swords.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِفَارِسٍ قَدْ ظَهَرَ مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-fārisin qad ẓahara min ʿaskari al-rūmi
sentences.l: And while they were like that, and behold, a horseman had appeared from the army of the Rūm.
sentences.i: While they were so engaged, a rider came out from the army of the Rūm.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: after this idhā of surprise the bi- simply marks what appears.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبَ رَأَوْهُ رَاكِبًا عَلَى بَغْلَةٍ قَطُوفٍ تَفِرُّ بِصَاحِبِهَا مِنْ وَقْعِ السُّيُوفِ وَبَرْذَعَتُهَا مِنْ أَبْيَضِ الْحَرِيرِ وَعَلَيْهَا سَجَّادَةٌ مِنْ شُغْلِ كَشْمِيرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaruba raʾawhu rākiban ʿalā baghlatin qaṭūfin tafirru bi-ṣāḥibihā min waqʿi al-suyūfi wa-bardhaʿatuhā min abyaḍi al-ḥarīri wa-ʿalayhā sajjādatun min shughli kashmīra
sentences.l: And when he drew near, they saw him riding on a she-mule, short-stepping, that flees with her owner from the falling of the swords; and her saddle-cloth was of the white of the silk, and on her a prayer-rug of the work of Kashmir.
sentences.i: As he came close they saw that he rode a short-paced mule, the kind that carries its rider away from the clash of swords, with a saddle-cloth of white silk and over it a prayer rug of Kashmir work.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: qaṭūf / suyūf, ḥarīr / kashmīr. A qaṭūf beast takes short, close steps; the mule is a mount for a man of religion, not for a warrior.

sentences.t: وَعَلَى ظَهْرِهَا شَيْخٌ مَلِيحُ الشَّيْبَةِ ظَاهِرُ الْهَيْبَةِ عَلَيْهِ مِدْرَعَةٌ مِنَ الصُّوفِ الْأَبْيَضِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalā ẓahrihā shaykhun malīḥu al-shaybati ẓāhiru al-haybati ʿalayhi midraʿatun mina al-ṣūfi al-abyaḍi
sentences.l: And on her back an old-man, comely of the grey-hair, manifest of the awe, on him a woollen-gown of the white wool.
sentences.i: On her back sat an old man with handsome white hair and a manifest air of dignity, dressed in a gown of white wool.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: shayba / hayba. A woollen midraʿa is the dress of the ascetic, and so the rider presents himself.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُسْرِعُ بِهَا وَيَنْهَضُ حَتَّى قَرُبَ مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal yusriʿu bihā wa-yanhaḍu ḥattā qaruba min ʿaskari al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And he did not cease hurrying with her and pressing-on until he drew near to the army of the Muslims.
sentences.i: He kept urging her on at speed until he was close to the Muslim army.
sentences.n: lam yazal with an imperfect, “he kept on doing”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِنِّي رَسُولٌ إِلَيْكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ وَمَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ فَأَعْطُونِي الْأَمَانَ وَالْإِقَالَهَ حَتَّى أُبَلِّغَكُمُ الرِّسَالَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla innī rasūlun ilaykum ajmaʿīna wa-mā ʿalā al-rasūli illā al-balāghu fa-aʿṭūnī al-amāna wa-al-iqālaha ḥattā uballighakumu al-risālata
sentences.l: And he said: I am a messenger to you all together, and there is not upon the messenger except the delivering; so give me the safe-conduct and the release until I deliver to you the message.
sentences.i: And he said, “I am an envoy to you all, and the messenger’s only duty is to deliver. So grant me safe-conduct and leave to speak freely, that I may deliver my message to you.”
sentences.n: wa-mā ʿalā al-rasūli illā al-balāghu is a phrase of the Qurʾān (5:99, 24:54), where the Messenger is the Prophet; the monk borrows it for himself as envoy. The print writes al-iqāla, “release, discharge” (here immunity for what he is about to say), with ه for the ending ة, a habit of the edition; it is kept and read as the ending.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ شَرْكَانُ لَكَ الْأَمَانُ فَلَا تَخْشَ حَرْبَ سَيْفٍ وَلَا طَعْنَ سِنَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu sharrukānu laka al-amānu fa-lā takhsha ḥarba sayfin wa-lā ṭaʿna sinānin
sentences.l: So Sharrukān said to him: To you the safe-conduct; so do not fear the war of a sword nor the thrust of a spearhead.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said to him, “You have safe-conduct: fear neither the stroke of sword nor the thrust of spear.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: amān … sinān. lā takhsha is the jussive of khashiya “fear”, its final long vowel cut short after the lā of prohibition.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَرَجَّلَ الشَّيْخُ وَقَلَعَ الصَّلِيبَ مِنْ عُنُقِهِ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ السُّلْطَانِ وَخَضَعَ لَهُ خُضُوعَ رَاجِى الْإِحْسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika tarajjala al-shaykhu wa-qalaʿa al-ṣalība min ʿunuqihi bayna yaday al-sulṭāni wa-khaḍaʿa lahu khuḍūʿa rājī al-iḥsāni
sentences.l: And at that the old man dismounted, and pulled off the cross from his neck between the two hands of the sultan, and humbled himself to him with the humbling of a hoper of kindness.
sentences.i: At that the old man got down from his mule, took the cross from his neck in the sultan’s presence, and bowed low before him as one who hopes for favour.
sentences.n: The print writes ى for final ي (yaday, rājī), a habit of the edition kept throughout. bayna yaday, “between the two hands of”, means “in the presence of”. khaḍaʿa lahu khuḍūʿa …: the verb with its own verbal noun, “humbled himself with the humbling of …”, says how he did it. Rhymed prose: sulṭān … iḥsān.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مَا مَعَكَ مِنَ الْأَخْبَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-muslimūna mā maʿaka mina al-akhbāri
sentences.l: So the Muslims said to him: What is with you of the tidings?
sentences.i: The Muslims said to him, “What news do you bring?”
sentences.n: qāla stands in the singular before its plural subject al-muslimūna: a verb that comes first does not take the plural.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ فَإِنِّي نَصَحْتُهُ لِيَمْتَنِعَ عَنْ تَلَفِ هَذِهِ الصُّوَرِ الْإِنْسَانِيَّةِ وَالْهَيَاكِلِ الرَّحْمَانِيَّةِ وَبَيَّنْتُ لَهُ أَنَّ الصَّوَابَ حَقْنُ الدِّمَاءِ وَالِاقْتِصَارُ عَلَى فَارِسَيْنِ فِى الْهَيْجَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla innī rasūlun min ʿindi al-maliki afrīdūna fa-innī naṣaḥtuhu li-yamtaniʿa ʿan talafi hādhihi al-ṣuwari al-insāniyyati wa-al-hayākili al-raḥmāniyyati wa-bayyantu lahu anna al-ṣawāba ḥaqnu al-dimāʾi wa-al-iqtiṣāru ʿalā fārisayni fī al-hayjāʾi
sentences.l: So he said: I am a messenger from with King Afrīdūn; for I counselled him so that he would refrain from the destruction of these human forms and the Merciful-made frames, and I made clear to him that the right thing is the sparing of the bloods and the limiting to two horsemen in the fray.
sentences.i: He said, “I am an envoy from King Afrīdūn. I counselled him to forbear from destroying these human forms, these frames fashioned by the Merciful, and showed him that the right course is to spare blood and leave it to two champions in the fray.”
sentences.n: al-hayākil al-raḥmāniyya, “the frames of the Merciful”: bodies as temples built by God (al-Raḥmān); rhymed with al-ṣuwar al-insāniyya. ḥaqn al-dimāʾ, literally “holding back the bloods”, is the stock phrase for sparing lives. fārisayni is the dual: a single combat of one champion from each side. The print writes fī with ى, as usual.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابَنِي إِلَى ذَلِكَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي فَدَيْتُ عَسْكَرِي بِرُوحِي فَلْيَفْعَلْ مَلِكُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِثْلِي وَيَفْدِي عَسْكَرَهُ بِرُوحِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābanī ilā dhālika wa-huwa yaqūlu lakum innī fadaytu ʿaskarī bi-rūḥī fa-l-yafʿal maliku al-muslimīna mithlī wa-yafdī ʿaskarahu bi-rūḥihi
sentences.l: So he answered me to that, and he says to you: I have ransomed my army with my soul; so let the king of the Muslims do like me and ransom his army with his soul.
sentences.i: He agreed to it, and he sends you word: “I offer my own life as ransom for my army; let the king of the Muslims do as I do and stake his life for his.”
sentences.n: ajāba ilā, “consent to”: the verb chooses the ilā. fadā bi-, “ransom (someone) with”: the bi- marks the price paid. fa-l-yafʿal is the jussive with the lām of command, “let him do”; Classical Arabic would carry the jussive on to the next verb, yafdi, but the print has yafdī with its long vowel, as the spoken language does, and it is kept.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ قَتَلَنِي فَلَا يَبْقَى لِعَسْكَرِ الْكُفَّارِ ثَبَاتٌ وَإِنْ قَتَلْتُهُ فَلَا يَبْقَى لِعَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ ثَبَاتٌ
sentences.tr: fa-in qatalanī fa-lā yabqā li-ʿaskari al-kuffāri thabātun wa-in qataltuhu fa-lā yabqā li-ʿaskari al-islāmi thabātun
sentences.l: So if he kills me, then there remains not to the army of the unbelievers a standing-firm; and if I kill him, then there remains not to the army of Islam a standing-firm.
sentences.i: “If he kills me, the army of the unbelievers will have no heart left to stand; and if I kill him, the army of Islam will have none.”
sentences.n: Afrīdūn, through the monk, calls his own side “the unbelievers”: the storyteller’s vocabulary, not the speaker’s. yabqā li-, “remain to, be left to”: the li- marks whose it is.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ يَا رَاهِبُ إِنَّا أَجَبْنَاهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ هَذَا هُوَ الْإِنْصَافُ فَلَا يَكُنْ مِنْهُ خِلَافٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa sharrukānu hādhā al-kalāma qāla yā rāhibu innā ajabnāhu ilā dhālika fa-inna hādhā huwa al-inṣāfu fa-lā yakun minhu khilāfun
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān heard this speech, he said: O monk, we have answered him to that, for this is the fairness; so let there not be from it a departing.
sentences.i: When Sharrukān heard this he said, “Monk, we accept it, for this is fair dealing, and there shall be no going back on it.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: inṣāf … khilāf. fa-lā yakun is the jussive of kāna after lā, “let there not be”.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَبْرُزُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَحْمِلُ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنِّي فَارِسُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهُوَ فَارِسُ الْكَافِرِينَ فَإِنْ قَتَلْتَنِي فَازَ بِالظَّفَرِ وَلَا يَبْقَى لِعَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ غَيْرُ الْمَفَرِّ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā abruzu ilayhi wa-aḥmilu ʿalayhi fa-innī fārisu al-muslimīna wa-huwa fārisu al-kāfirīna fa-in qataltanī fāza bi-al-ẓafari wa-lā yabqā li-ʿaskari al-muslimīna ghayru al-mafarri
sentences.l: And here I am, I go out to him and charge upon him, for I am the horseman of the Muslims and he is the horseman of the unbelievers; so if you kill me, he has won the victory, and there remains not to the army of the Muslims other than the fleeing.
sentences.i: “Here I am: I will go out to meet him and charge him, for I am the champion of the Muslims and he the champion of the unbelievers. If I am killed, the victory is his, and nothing is left for the Muslim army but flight.”
sentences.n: The print has qataltanī, “(if) you kill me”, though the next verb is “he has won”; one expects qatalanī “he kills me”, as in the monk’s message, and the print may be at fault, but this is uncertain, so it is kept and read as addressed to the monk’s side. baraza ilā “go out to (single combat)”; ḥamala ʿalā “charge upon”: the verbs choose the prepositions. fāza bi-, “win”: the bi- marks the prize.

sentences.t: فَارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ أَيُّهَا الرَّاهِبُ وَقُلْ لَهُ إِنَّ الْبِرَازَ يَكُونُ فِي غَدٍ لِأَنَّنَا أَتَيْنَا مِنْ سَفَرِنَا عَلَى تَعَبٍ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَبَعْدَ الرَّاحَةِ لَاعَتْبَ وَلَا لَوْمَ
sentences.tr: fa-irjiʿ ilayhi ayyuhā al-rāhibu wa-qul lahu inna al-birāza yakūnu fī ghadin li-annanā ataynā min safarinā ʿalā taʿabin fī hādhā al-yawmi wa-baʿda al-rāḥati lā ʿatba wa-lā lawma
sentences.l: So go back to him, O monk, and say to him: The single-combat will be on the morrow, because we have come from our journey upon weariness on this day; and after the rest, no reproach and no blame.
sentences.i: “So go back to him, monk, and tell him the combat will be tomorrow, for we arrived today weary from our march; once we are rested, let there be no reproach and no blame.”
sentences.n: The print runs lā ʿatba together as one word, لاعتب; the spacing is kept. lā ʿatba wa-lā lawma: lā denying a whole class takes its noun in the accusative without nunation, “no reproach at all”.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَ الرَّاهِبُ وَهُوَ مَسْرُورٌ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَمَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَأَخْبَرَهُمَا بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿa al-rāhibu wa-huwa masrūrun ḥattā waṣala ilā al-maliki afrīdūna wa-maliki al-rūmi wa-akhbarahumā bi-dhālika
sentences.l: So the monk returned, and he glad, until he reached King Afrīdūn and the king of the Rūm, and informed them both of that.
sentences.i: The monk went back rejoicing to King Afrīdūn and the king of the Rūm, and told them both.
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-, which marks the news told.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ وَزَالَ عَنْهُ الْهَمُّ وَالتَّرَحُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-maliku afrīdūnu ghāyata al-faraḥi wa-zāla ʿanhu al-hammu wa-al-taraḥu
sentences.l: And King Afrīdūn rejoiced the utmost of rejoicing, and there passed from him the care and the grief.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn was overjoyed, and all his care and sorrow left him.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: faraḥ … taraḥ, “joy … grief”, a stock jingle. ghāyata al-faraḥi, “the utmost of joy”, is an adverbial accusative of degree.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ لَا شَكَّ أَنَّ شَرْكَانَ هَذَا هُوَ أَضْرَبُهُمْ بِالسَّيْفِ وَأَطْعَنُهُمْ بِالسِّنَانِ فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُهُ انْكَسَرَتْ هِمَّتُهُمْ وَضَعُفَتْ قُوَّتُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi lā shakka anna sharrukāna hādhā huwa aḍrabuhum bi-al-sayfi wa-aṭʿanuhum bi-al-sināni fa-idhā qataltuhu inkasarat himmatuhum wa-ḍaʿufat quwwatuhum
sentences.l: And he said in his soul: No doubt that this Sharrukān, he is the best-striking of them with the sword and the best-thrusting of them with the spearhead; so when I have killed him, their resolve will be broken and their strength will weaken.
sentences.i: And he said to himself, “No doubt this Sharrukān is the finest of them all with sword and spear; once I have killed him, their spirit will break and their strength will fail.”
sentences.n: aḍrabuhum, aṭʿanuhum: elatives (“most …”) of ḍaraba “strike” and ṭaʿana “thrust”, “the best striker, the best thruster of them”. bi- here is “with”, the instrument. After fa-idhā the perfect looks forward: “when I have killed him”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَانَتْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي كَاتَبَتِ الْمَلِكَ أَفْرِيدُونَ بِذَلِكَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ هُوَ فَارِسُ الشُّجْعَانِ وَشُجَاعُ الْفُرْسَانِ وَحَذَّرَتْ أَفْرِيدُونَ مِنْ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-qad kānat dhātu al-dawāhī kātabati al-malika afrīdūna bi-dhālika wa-qālat lahu inna sharrukāna huwa fārisu al-shujʿāni wa-shujāʿu al-fursāni wa-ḥadhdharat afrīdūna min sharrukāna
sentences.l: And Dhāt al-Dawāhī had written to King Afrīdūn about that, and said to him: Sharrukān, he is the horseman of the brave and the brave one of the horsemen; and she warned Afrīdūn of Sharrukān.
sentences.i: Dhāt al-Dawāhī had already written to King Afrīdūn about this, telling him that Sharrukān was the champion among the brave and the bravest of the champions, and she had warned Afrīdūn against him.
sentences.n: qad kānat … kātabat, “had written”: kāna with a perfect makes a pluperfect. kātaba bi-, “write to (someone) about”: the bi- marks the matter. fāris al-shujʿān wa-shujāʿ al-fursān is a chiasmus, the two words trading places.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَفْرِيدُونُ فَارِسًا عَظِيمًا لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يُقَاتِلُ أَنْوَاعَ الْقِتَالِ وَيَرْمِي بِالْحِجَارَةِ وَالنِّبَالِ وَيَضْرِبُ بِعَمُودِ الْحَدِيدِ وَلَا يَخْشَى مِنَ الْبَأْسِ الشَّدِيدِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna afrīdūnu fārisan ʿaẓīman li-annahu kāna yuqātilu anwāʿa al-qitāli wa-yarmī bi-al-ḥijārati wa-al-nibāli wa-yaḍribu bi-ʿamūdi al-ḥadīdi wa-lā yakhshā mina al-baʾsi al-shadīdi
sentences.l: And Afrīdūn was a mighty horseman, because he used to fight the kinds of fighting, and shoot with the stones and the arrows, and strike with the column of the iron, and not fear of the fierce might.
sentences.i: Afrīdūn was a mighty horseman: he could fight in every manner of combat, sling stones and shoot arrows, lay about him with an iron mace, and feared no violence however fierce.
sentences.n: kāna with the imperfect (kāna yuqātilu) describes habit or ability. ʿamūd al-ḥadīd, “the column of iron”, is the iron mace. ramā bi-, “throw, shoot”: the bi- marks the missile. Rhymed prose: nibāl … qitāl, ḥadīd … shadīd. yakhshā min, “fear (of)”: the min is the spoken usage; khashiya normally takes a direct object.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَفْرِيدُونُ قَوْلَ الرَّاهِبِ مِنْ أَنَّ شَرْكَانَ أَجَابَ إِلَى الْبِرَازِ كَادَأَنْ يَطِيرَ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ لِأَنَّهُ وَاثِقٌ بِنَفْسِهِ وَيَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ لَاطَاقَةَ لِأَحَدٍ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa afrīdūnu qawla al-rāhibi min anna sharrukāna ajāba ilā al-birāzi kāda an yaṭīra min shiddati al-faraḥi li-annahu wāthiqun bi-nafsihi wa-yaʿlamu annahu lā ṭāqata li-aḥadin bihi
sentences.l: And when Afrīdūn heard the speech of the monk, of that Sharrukān had answered to the single-combat, he almost was to fly from the intensity of the joy, because he is trusting in himself and knows that there is no power to anyone against him.
sentences.i: When Afrīdūn heard from the monk that Sharrukān had accepted the combat, he nearly flew for joy, for he trusted in himself and knew that no one could stand against him.
sentences.n: The print joins kāda an as one word, كادان, and lā ṭāqata as لاطاقة; the spacing is kept. min anna, “to the effect that”: the min introduces the content of what was said. lā ṭāqata li-aḥadin bihi, “no power to anyone over him”: li- marks who lacks the power, bi- what it is against. wāthiq bi-, “trusting in”: the participle chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَاتَ الْكُفَّارُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ فِي فَرَحٍ وَسُرُورٍ وَشُرْبِ خُمُورٍ
sentences.tr: thumma bāta al-kuffāru tilka al-laylata fī faraḥin wa-surūrin wa-shurbi khumūrin
sentences.l: Then the unbelievers passed that night in joy and gladness and the drinking of wines.
sentences.i: The unbelievers spent that night in joy and gladness, drinking wine.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: surūr … khumūr. tilka al-laylata is accusative of time, “that night”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الصَّبَاحُ أَقْبَلَتِ الْفَوَارِسُ بِسُمْرِ الرِّمَاحِ وَبِيضِ الصِّفَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-ṣabāḥu aqbalati al-fawārisu bi-sumri al-rimāḥi wa-bīḍi al-ṣifāḥi
sentences.l: And when it was the morning, the horsemen came forward with the brown of the lances and the white of the broad-blades.
sentences.i: When morning came the horsemen advanced with their tawny lances and their gleaming blades.
sentences.n: sumr al-rimāḥ, “the tawny ones of the lances”, and bīḍ al-ṣifāḥ, “the white ones of the blades”, are stock epithets: lances of brown cane, swords of bright steel. The bi- is “with”, what they carried. Rhymed prose: rimāḥ … ṣifāḥ.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا هُمْ بِفَارِسٍ قَدْ بَرَزَ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā hum bi-fārisin qad baraza fī al-maydāni
sentences.l: And behold, they, with a horseman who had come out into the field.
sentences.i: And behold, a horseman had ridden out into the field.
sentences.n: wa-idhā hum bi-…, “and behold, they (were faced) with …”: idhā of surprise, with bi- marking what suddenly appears.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ عَلَى جَوَادٍ مِنَ الْخَيْلِ الْجِيَادِ مُعَدٍّ لِلْحَرْبِ وَالْجِلَادِ وَلَهُ قَوَائِمُ شِدَادٌ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa rākibun ʿalā jawādin mina al-khayli al-jiyādi muʿaddin li-al-ḥarbi wa-al-jilādi wa-lahu qawāʾimu shidādun
sentences.l: And he was riding on a steed of the horses, the fine-ones, made-ready for war and the combat, and to-it were legs strong.
sentences.i: He was riding a steed of the finest breed, made ready for war and combat, and sturdy of leg.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-jiyād, al-jilād, shidād all fall on -ād. muʿaddin agrees with the horse, jawād.

sentences.t: وَعَلَى ذَلِكَ الْفَارِسِ دِرْعٌ مِنَ الْحَدِيدِ مُعَدٌّ لِلْبَأْسِ الشَّدِيدِ وَفِي صَدْرِهِ مِرْآةٌ مِنَ الْجَوْهَرِ وَفِي يَدِهِ صَارِمٌ أَبْتَرُ وَقِنْطَارِيَّةُ خُولَنْجٍ مِنْ غَرِيبِ عَمَلِ الْإِ فْرَنْجِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalā dhālika al-fārisi dirʿun mina al-ḥadīdi muʿaddun li-al-baʾsi al-shadīdi wa-fī ṣadrihi mirʾātun mina al-jawhari wa-fī yadihi ṣārimun abtaru wa-qinṭāriyyatu khūlanjin min gharībi ʿamali al-ifranji
sentences.l: And upon that horseman was a coat-of-mail of iron, made-ready for the might, the hard, and on his chest a mirror of jewels, and in his hand a sharp-blade, a cutting-one, and a lance of khūlanj, of the strange work of the Franks.
sentences.i: That knight wore a coat of iron mail, ready for the fiercest fighting; on his breast was a mirror set with gems, and in his hand a keen, trenchant sword and a lance of khūlanj wood, of rare Frankish workmanship.
sentences.n: The mirror is a polished breastplate-disc. khūlanj (Persian khalang) is a hard, speckled wood; reading qinṭāriyyatu khūlanjin as “a lance of khūlanj” is our best sense. The print splits al-Ifranj, “the Franks”, into الا and فرنج; both pieces are kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْفَارِسَ كَشَفَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ وَقَالَ مَنْ عَرَفَنِى فَقَدِ اكْتَفَانِى وَمَنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفْنِى فَسَوْفَ يَرَانِي أَنَا أَفْرِيدُونُ الْمَغْمُورُ بِبَرَكَةِ شَوَاهِي ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-fārisa kashafa ʿan wajhihi wa-qāla man ʿarafanī fa-qadi iktafānī wa-man lam yaʿrifnī fa-sawfa yarānī anā afrīdūnu al-maghmūru bi-barakati shawāhī dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: Then the horseman uncovered from his face and said: Whoever knows me, has had-enough-of-me; and whoever does not know me, then soon he will see me: I am Afrīdūn, the one-flooded with the blessing of Shawāhī, Dhāt al-Dawāhī!
sentences.i: Then the knight bared his face and said, “Whoever knows me needs no more of me, and whoever does not know me shall soon see me: I am Afrīdūn, steeped in the blessing of Shawāhī, Dhāt al-Dawāhī!”
sentences.n: The print has افربدزن, a misprint for افريدون, corrected here. The boast is a stock formula: whoever knows me “has had enough”, needs no introduction. Shawāhī is the old woman’s own name; Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “She of the Calamities”, is her byname. The print writes final ي as ى in عرفنى, اكتفانى, يعرفنى, as often.

sentences.t: فَمَا تَمَّ كَلَامُهُ حَتَّى خَرَجَ فِي وَجْهِهِ فَارِسُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā tamma kalāmuhu ḥattā kharaja fī wajhihi fārisu al-muslimīna sharrukānu
sentences.l: And his speech was not completed until there went out in his face the horseman of the Muslims, Sharrukān.
sentences.i: Hardly had he finished speaking when the champion of the Muslims, Sharrukān, came out to face him.
sentences.n: fa-mā … ḥattā, “not … until”: the usual way of saying “no sooner … than”.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ عَلَى جَوَادٍ أَشْقَرَ يُسَاوِى أَلْفًا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ وَعَلَيْهِ عُدَّةٌ مُزَرْكَشَةٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَهُوَ مُتَقَلِّدٌ بِسَيْفٍ هِنْدِىٍّ مُجَوْهَرٍ يَقُدُّ الرِّقَابَ وَيُهَوِّنُ الْأُمُورَ الصِّعَابَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa rākibun ʿalā jawādin ashqara yusāwī alfan mina al-dhahabi al-aḥmari wa-ʿalayhi ʿuddatun muzarkashatun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-huwa mutaqallidun bi-sayfin hindiyyin mujawharin yaquddu al-riqāba wa-yuhawwinu al-umūra al-ṣiʿāba
sentences.l: And he was riding on a steed, a chestnut, that was-worth a thousand of the gold, the red, and on him was gear embroidered with the pearls and the jewels, and he was girt with a sword, Indian, jewelled, that cleaves the necks and makes-easy the matters, the hard-ones.
sentences.i: He rode a chestnut horse worth a thousand pieces of red gold; he wore armour worked with pearls and gems, and was girt with a jewelled Indian sword that cleaves necks and makes hard things easy.
sentences.n: “A thousand of red gold”: a thousand dinars; red gold is pure gold. mutaqallid bi-, “girt with”: the bi- marks what is slung on. Rhymed prose: al-aḥmar / al-jawhar, al-riqāb / al-ṣiʿāb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَاقَ جَوَادَهُ بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ وَالْفُرْسَانُ تَنْظُرُهُ بِالْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma sāqa jawādahu bayna al-ṣaffayni wa-al-fursānu tanẓuruhu bi-al-ʿayni
sentences.l: Then he drove his steed between the two ranks, and the horsemen looking-at-him with the eye.
sentences.i: Then he rode his horse out between the two lines while the horsemen watched him.
sentences.n: al-fursān, a broken plural, takes a feminine-singular verb, tanẓuru.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَادَى أَفْرِيدُونَ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ يَا مَلْعُونُ أَتَظُنُّنِي كَمَنْ لَاقَيْتَ مِنَ الْفُرْسَانِ وَلَا يَثْبُتُ مَعَكَ فِي حَوْمَةِ الْمَيْدَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma nādā afrīdūna wa-qāla lahu waylaka yā malʿūnu a-taẓunnunī ka-man lāqayta mina al-fursāni wa-lā yathbutu maʿaka fī ḥawmati al-maydāni
sentences.l: Then he called Afrīdūn and said to him: Woe to you, O accursed! Do you think me like whom you have met of the horsemen and [who] does not stand-firm with you in the thick of the field?
sentences.i: Then he called out to Afrīdūn: “Woe to you, accursed one! Do you take me for one of the horsemen you have met, who cannot hold his ground against you in the thick of the field?”
sentences.n: The print has ينبت, a misprint for يثبت, corrected here. Sharrukān is the speaker; Afrīdūn is the object of nādā, “called”. ka-, “like”, governs man, “whoever”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ فَصَارَ الِاثْنَانِ كَأَنَّهُمَا جَبَلَانِ يَصْطَدِمَانِ أَوْ بَحْرَانِ يَلْتَطِمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamala kullun minhumā ʿalā ṣāḥibihi fa-ṣāra al-ithnāni ka-annahumā jabalāni yaṣṭadimāni aw baḥrāni yaltaṭimāni
sentences.l: Then charged each of the two of them upon his fellow, and the two became as-though they were two mountains colliding, or two seas dashing-together.
sentences.i: Then each charged the other, and the two were like two mountains crashing together or two seas whose waves clash.
sentences.n: ḥamala ʿalā, “charge at”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَارَبَا وَتَبَاعَدَا وَالْتَصَقَا وَافْتَرَقَا وَلَمْ يَزَ الَا فِى كَرٍّ وَفَرٍّ وَهَزْلٍ وَجِدٍّ وَضَرْبٍ وَطَعْنٍ
sentences.tr: thumma taqārabā wa-tabāʿadā wa-iltaṣaqā wa-iftaraqā wa-lam yazālā fī karrin wa-farrin wa-hazlin wa-jiddin wa-ḍarbin wa-ṭaʿnin
sentences.l: Then they drew-near and drew-apart, and clung-together and parted, and did not cease in charge and wheeling-away, and jest and earnest, and striking and thrusting.
sentences.i: They closed and drew apart, grappled and broke away, and kept on at it, charging and wheeling, feinting and fighting in earnest, striking and thrusting.
sentences.n: The print splits yazālā, “the two ceased”, as يز الا; both pieces are kept as printed and read together as lam yazālā, “they did not cease”. karr wa-farr, “attack and retreat”, is the stock phrase for cavalry fighting.

sentences.t: وَالْجَيْشَانِ يَنْظُرَانِ إِلَيْهِمَا وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ غَالِبٌ وَالْبَعْضُ يَقُولُ إِنَّ أَفْرِيدُونَ غَالِبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-al-jayshāni yanẓurāni ilayhimā wa-baʿḍuhum yaqūlu inna sharrukāna ghālibun wa-al-baʿḍu yaqūlu inna afrīdūna ghālibun
sentences.l: And the two armies looking at the two of them, and some of them saying: Sharrukān is winning, and the some saying: Afrīdūn is winning.
sentences.i: Both armies watched them, some saying Sharrukān had the upper hand and others that Afrīdūn had.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْفَارِسَانِ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ حَتَّى بَطَلَ الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ وَعَلَا الْغُبَارُ وَوَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَمَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ إِلَى الِاصْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-fārisāni ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli ḥattā baṭala al-qīlu wa-al-qālu wa-ʿalā al-ghubāru wa-wallā al-nahāru wa-mālati al-shamsu ilā al-iṣfirāri
sentences.l: And the two horsemen did not cease on this state until the it-is-said and the he-said ceased, and the dust rose, and the day turned-away, and the sun inclined to the yellowing.
sentences.i: The two knights went on like this until all the talk died away, the dust rose high, the day was spent and the sun leaned toward its yellowing.
sentences.n: ḥāl is taken as masculine here (hādhā al-ḥāl), as often in this text. Rhymed prose: al-ghubār / al-nahār / al-iṣfirār. al-qīl wa-al-qāl, “talk and chatter”: the onlookers fall silent.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ عَلَى شَرْكَانَ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَحَقِّ دِينِ الْمَسِيحِ وَالِاعْتِقَادِ الصَّحِيحِ مَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا فَارِسٌ كَرَّارٌ وَبَطَلٌ مِغْوَارٌ غَيْرَ أَنَّكَ غَدَّارٌ وَطَبْعُكَ مَا هُوَ طَبْعُ الْأَخْيَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa al-maliku afrīdūnu ʿalā sharrukāna wa-qāla lahu wa-ḥaqqi dīni al-masīḥi wa-al-iʿtiqādi al-ṣaḥīḥi mā anta illā fārisun karrārun wa-baṭalun mighwārun ghayra annaka ghaddārun wa-ṭabʿuka mā huwa ṭabʿu al-akhyāri
sentences.l: And King Afrīdūn shouted at Sharrukān and said to him: By the right of the religion of the Messiah and the belief, the true, you are nothing but a horseman oft-charging and a hero bold-raiding, except that you are treacherous, and your nature, it is not the nature of the good.
sentences.i: Then King Afrīdūn shouted to Sharrukān, “By the religion of the Messiah and the true faith, you are a knight who charges again and again, a daring hero, but you are treacherous; your nature is not that of the noble.
sentences.n: ṣāḥa ʿalā, “shout at”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. wa-ḥaqqi, “by the right of”, opens an oath; the wa- is the oath particle and takes the genitive. karrār, mighwār, ghaddār are intensive patterns: one who does the thing over and over. Afrīdūn is setting up a trick.

sentences.t: لِأَنِّي أَرَى فِعْلَكَ غَيْرَ حَمِيدٍ وَقِتَالُكَ قِتَالُ الصِّنْدِيدِ وَقَوْمُكَ يَنْسُبُونَكَ إِلَى الْعَبِيدِ
sentences.tr: li-annī arā fiʿlaka ghayra ḥamīdin wa-qitāluka qitālu al-ṣindīdi wa-qawmuka yansubūnaka ilā al-ʿabīdi
sentences.l: Because I see your doing not praiseworthy, and your fighting is the fighting of the champion, and your people attribute you to the slaves.
sentences.i: For I see that your conduct is blameworthy, though you fight like a true champion, and your own people count you among the slaves.
sentences.n: nasaba ilā, “trace back to, count among”: the verb chooses the ilā. The charge is invented: Afrīdūn wants Sharrukān to think his men are slighting him.

sentences.t: وَهَاهُمْ أَخْرَجُوالَكَ غَيْرَ جَوَادِكَ وَتَعُودُ إِلَى الْقِتَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-hāhum akhrajū laka ghayra jawādika wa-taʿūdu ilā al-qitāli
sentences.l: And here-they-are, they have brought out for you other than your steed, and you will return to the fighting.
sentences.i: See, they have brought out a fresh horse for you, and you will come back to the fight on it.
sentences.n: The print runs akhrajū and laka together as اخرجوالك, and writes hā hum, “here they are”, as one word; both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي وَحَقِّ دِينِي قَدْ أَعْيَانِي قِتَالُكَ وَأَتْعَبَنِي ضَرْبُكَ وَطِعَانُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-innī wa-ḥaqqi dīnī qad aʿyānī qitāluka wa-atʿabanī ḍarbuka wa-ṭiʿānuka
sentences.l: And I, by the right of my religion, your fighting has wearied me, and your striking and your thrusting have tired me.
sentences.i: As for me, by my faith, fighting you has worn me out, and your blows and thrusts have exhausted me.
sentences.n: wa-innī, “and I”, is left hanging when the oath breaks in, and the sentence goes on with a new subject: a loose, spoken construction.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ قِتَالِي فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ فَلَا تُغَيِّرْ شَيْأً مِنْ عُدَّتِكَ وَلَا جَوَادَكَ حَتَّى يَظْهَرَ لِلْفُرْسَانِ كَرَمُكَ وَقِتَالُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta turīdu qitālī fī hādhihi al-laylati fa-lā tughayyir shayʾan min ʿuddatika wa-lā jawādaka ḥattā yaẓhara li-al-fursāni karamuka wa-qitāluka
sentences.l: So if you were wanting my fighting in this night, then do not change a thing of your gear nor your steed, so that may appear to the horsemen your nobility and your fighting.
sentences.i: So if you want to fight me tonight, change nothing of your armour or your horse, so that the knights may see your nobility and your prowess.”
sentences.n: The print spells shayʾan as شيأ, with the hamza on the alif of the accusative.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ اغْتَاظَ مِنْ قَوْلِ أَصْحَابِهِ فِي حَقِّهِ حَيْثُ يَنْسُبُونَهُ إِلَى الْعَبِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa sharrukānu hādhā al-kalāma ightāẓa min qawli aṣḥābihi fī ḥaqqihi ḥaythu yansubūnahu ilā al-ʿabīdi
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān heard this speech, he was enraged at the saying of his companions about him, since they attribute him to the slaves.
sentences.i: When Sharrukān heard this, he was furious at what his men were saying about him, counting him among the slaves.
sentences.n: fī ḥaqqihi, literally “in his right”: “concerning him”.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِمْ شَرْكَانُ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يُشِيرَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَيَأْمُرَهُمْ أَنْ لَا يُغَيِّرُوا لَهُ جَوَادًا وَلَاعُدَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ilayhim sharrukānu wa-arāda an yushīra ilayhim wa-yaʾmurahum an lā yughayyirū lahu jawādan wa-lā ʿuddatan
sentences.l: So Sharrukān turned to them, and wanted to signal to them and command them that they not change for him a steed nor gear.
sentences.i: Sharrukān turned toward them, meaning to signal them and order them not to change his horse or his armour.
sentences.n: The print runs wa-lā and ʿuddatan together as ولاعدّة; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِأَفْرِيدُونَ هَزَّ حَرْبَتَهُ وَأَرْسَلَهَا إِلَى شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-afrīdūna hazza ḥarbatahu wa-arsalahā ilā sharrukāna
sentences.l: And behold, Afrīdūn shook his spear and sent it at Sharrukān.
sentences.i: At that moment Afrīdūn brandished his spear and hurled it at Sharrukān.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ وَرَاءَهُ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ أَحَدًا فَعَلِمَ أَنَّهَا حِيلَةٌ مِنَ الْمَلْعُونِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata warāʾahu fa-lam yajid aḥadan fa-ʿalima annahā ḥīlatun mina al-malʿūni
sentences.l: And he turned behind him and did not find anyone, and knew that it was a trick from the accursed.
sentences.i: He looked behind him and saw no one, and realised it was a ruse of the accursed man.

sentences.t: فَرَدَّ وَجْهَهُ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَإِذَا بِالْحَرْبَةِ قَدْأَ دْرَكَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-radda wajhahu bi-surʿatin wa-idhā bi-al-ḥarbati qad adrakathu
sentences.l: So he turned back his face with speed, and behold, the spear had reached him.
sentences.i: He turned his face back quickly, and there was the spear, already upon him.
sentences.n: The print sets qad adrakathu, “had reached him”, as قدا دركته, with the a- of the verb attached to qad; both pieces are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَمَالَ عَنْهَا حَتَّى سَاوَى بِرَأْسِهِ قَرَبُوصَ سَرْجِهِ فَجَرَتِ الْحَرْبَةُ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-māla ʿanhā ḥattā sāwā bi-raʾsihi qarabūṣa sarjihi fa-jarati al-ḥarbatu ʿalā ṣadrihi
sentences.l: And he leaned away from it until he made-level his head with the pommel of his saddle, and the spear ran along his chest.
sentences.i: He swerved away from it, bending until his head was level with the pommel of his saddle, and the spear grazed along his chest.
sentences.n: The print spells qarabūs, “saddle-bow, pommel”, with ṣād, قربوص, a known variant. sāwā bi-, “bring level with”: the bi- marks what he brings down, his head.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ شَرْكَانُ عَالِىَ الصَّدْرِ فَكَشَطَتِ الْحَرْبَةُ جِلْدَةَ صَدْرِهِ فَصَاحَ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً وَغَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna sharrukānu ʿāliya al-ṣadri fa-kashaṭati al-ḥarbatu jildata ṣadrihi fa-ṣāḥa ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan wa-ghāba ʿani al-dunyā
sentences.l: And Sharrukān was high of the chest, so the lance scraped-off the skin of his chest, and he cried a single cry and was absent from the world.
sentences.i: Sharrukān was deep-chested, so the lance tore away the skin of his breast; he gave one cry and lost his senses.
sentences.n: ʿālī al-ṣadr, “high of chest”: his chest stood forward, so the lance caught it. The print writes final ي as ى, a habit of the edition throughout (عالى for عالي). ghāba ʿan al-dunyā, “was absent from the world”, means he fainted, not that he died.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلْعُونُ أَفْرِيدُونُ بِذَلِكَ وَعَرَفَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ قَتَلَهُ فَصَاحَ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ وَنَادَى بِالْفَرَحِ فَهَاجَتْ أَهْلُ الطُّغْيَانِ وَبَكَتْ أَهْلُ الْإِيمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-malʿūnu afrīdūnu bi-dhālika wa-ʿarafa annahu qad qatalahu fa-ṣāḥa ʿalā al-kuffāri wa-nādā bi-al-faraḥi fa-hājat ahlu al-ṭughyāni wa-bakat ahlu al-īmāni
sentences.l: And the accursed Afrīdūn rejoiced at that, and knew that he had killed him; so he shouted to the unbelievers and called-out with joy; and the people of the tyranny surged, and the people of the faith wept.
sentences.i: The accursed Afrīdūn rejoiced at this, sure that he had killed him, and he shouted to the unbelievers and called out in his joy; the people of tyranny surged forward, and the people of faith wept.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-ṭughyān / al-īmān. fariḥa bi-, “rejoice at”: the verb chooses the bi-. ahl “people” is masculine, but the verbs here are feminine (hājat, bakat), treating the crowd as a collective; Afrīdūn only thinks Sharrukān is dead.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّارَأَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ أَخَاهُ مَائِلًا عَلَى الْجَوَادِ حَتَّى كَادَ أَنْ يَقَعَ أَرْسَلَ نَحْوَهُ الْفُرْسَانَ فَتَسَابَقَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْأَبْطَالُ وَأَتَوابِهِ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā ḍawʾu al-makāni akhāhu māʾilan ʿalā al-jawādi ḥattā kāda an yaqaʿa arsala naḥwahu al-fursāna fa-tasābaqat ilayhi al-abṭālu wa-ataw bihi ilayhi
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw his-brother leaning on the steed until he was about to fall, he sent toward him the horsemen; and the champions raced-one-another to him, and they came with-him to-him.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw his brother slumped over his horse and about to fall, he sent the horsemen to him; the champions raced each other to reach him, and they brought him back to his brother.
sentences.n: The print runs فلما and رأى together (فلمارأى), and وأتوا and به together (واتوابه); the spacing is kept. atā bi-, “bring”: the verb chooses the bi-, so “they came with him to him” means they brought Sharrukān to Ḍawʾ al-Makān. kāda an yaqaʿa, “he was about to fall”.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَتِ الْكُفَّارُ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالْتَقَى الْجَيْشَانِ وَاخْتَلَطَ الصَّفَّانِ وَعَمِلَ الْيَمَانِيُّ الْبَتَّارُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamalati al-kuffāru ʿalā al-muslimīna wa-iltaqā al-jayshāni wa-ikhtalaṭa al-ṣaffāni wa-ʿamila al-yamāniyyu al-battāru
sentences.l: And the unbelievers charged upon the Muslims, and the two armies met, and the two ranks mingled, and the Yemeni, the cutting, worked.
sentences.i: Then the unbelievers charged the Muslims, the two armies met, the two lines were mingled together, and the keen Yemeni blade did its work.
sentences.n: ḥamala ʿalā, “charge, attack”. al-yamānī al-battār, “the Yemeni, the cutting”, is the sword, named by its famous origin; the noun itself is left out.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَسْبَقَ النَّاسِ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna asbaqa al-nāsi ilā sharrukāna al-wazīru dandānu
sentences.l: And the quickest of the people to Sharrukān was the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: And the first of them all to reach Sharrukān was the vizier Dandān.
sentences.n: The predicate comes first and the subject last: kāna asbaqa al-nāsi … al-wazīru dandānu, “the vizier Dandān was the quickest of the people”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
